course: CSC3209 Software Architecture and Design Patterns

non_top_level_terms.scalability: quality concern outside the seven-category exam answer set
non_top_level_terms.flexibility: broad quality/property; use the course category justified by the scenario
non_top_level_terms.maintainability: related term; use Modifiability for the course top-level category
non_top_level_terms.reliability: broad quality/property; do not substitute it for Availability without a service-continuity scenario
non_top_level_terms.consistency: data/coordination property, not one of the seven top-level categories
non_top_level_terms.complexity: cost or weakness, not one of the seven top-level categories
non_top_level_terms.reuse: architectural benefit, not one of the seven top-level categories

source_notes.claim: Client-Server factors common services into one or a small number of locations to promote Modifiability and reuse; centralized control is the mechanism, not a top-level QA. Availability additionally depends on distributing resources across physical servers.
Map-Reduce parallelism targets Performance; framework overhead and partition imbalance can erase that Performance benefit.
Multi-Tier can support Security, Performance, Availability and Modifiability; its stated weakness is cost and complexity, which must be labelled as a weakness rather than a top-level QA.
